core_obligations: Case outside Z (proof lines 6661-6667): for a geometric point of X with image in the open complement U of Z, the author shows that the stalk of i_{small,*}G is a singleton, because a neighbourhood of the point meeting Z can be shrunk away from Z.

Case inside Z (proof lines 6670-6699): for a geometric point lying over Z, the author identifies the stalk of i_{small,*}G with the stalk of G at the same geometric point, using the description of the stalk as a filtered colimit over etale neighbourhoods and the comparison of the etale sites of Z and X at the point.
Both cases together give the displayed computation of the statement.
proof_roadmap: For a point outside Z, shrink a neighbourhood away from Z to see the stalk is a singleton.
For a point inside Z, compare the filtered colimits defining the two stalks.
Collect the two cases into the displayed formula.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the stalks of the pushforward of a sheaf along a closed immersion: the stalk is a singleton at geometric points outside Z and the stalk of the original sheaf at geometric points inside Z (statement lines 6643-6659). The proof treats the two cases separately: outside Z the author uses that an etale neighbourhood can be shrunk away from Z (proof lines 6661-6667), and inside Z the stalk is identified through the comparison of the filtered colimits defining both stalks (proof lines 6670-6699). The non-formal content is the comparison in the second case. The claim is H2: two short computations.
